tools.description: Start here to select authorized immutable publications, or refresh after material_unavailable. Costs 0 calls, including every directory page, even when content credits are exhausted. items contains name, published_book_ref (book_id + publication_id), is_default and available_tools for each publication. Copy a selected reference into content arguments and choose an available tool. An empty directory means this account has no authorized materials; ask the user to contact the administrator. complete=false means more items exist: copy next_calls name and arguments for needed pages. Returns usage without a charge; directory entries are not evidence and have no source citations.

after.description: Omit for the first page; copy the after reference from book_list next_calls for later pages.

publication_id.description: Exact publication version returned by book_list.

limit.description: Maximum publications on this directory page.

tools.name: book_list

tools.description: Read canonical source text by one LID or an inclusive LID range. Use when: Read source text after a LID has been located. Do not use for lexical discovery when no LID is known.  Returns data.text with at most 8,000 Unicode characters per page, data.source_range for this page and data.requested_range for the requested LIDs. Ranges are absolute canonical-source UTF-16 [start, end), not byte offsets. Preserve the publication and range when continuing. Copy published_book_ref from book_list and check its available_tools. Costs 1 call on success, including empty results, each continuation page and repeated successful requests; failures cost 0. complete=false means more pages exist; copy needed next_calls name and arguments unchanged. sources gives published_book_ref, start_lid/end_lid, source_range and source_url: cite only evidence actually read, retaining its version and exact range. An empty sources array provides no source citation. usage is the server's post-call balance with charged_units and charged_from; do not infer balance locally. On quota_exhausted stop content retries and report usage.free_resets_at plus top_up_url or top_up_instruction; book_list and mcp_usage remain free.

end_lid.description: Inclusive final LID in source reading order; for a search hit, use end_lid. Reads from lid's span start through end_lid's span end. Omit or null to read only lid's span.

lid.description: Known LID from this book's locating or structure results; for a search hit, use start_lid. Reads the node's canonical source span, including descendants.

published_book_ref.description: Copy the exact immutable publication reference from book_list; keep both identifiers on every content call and continuation.

publication_id.description: Exact publication version returned by book_list.

start_utf16.description: Absolute canonical-source UTF-16 position from next_calls; omit for the first page.

tools.name: book_text

tools.description: Enumerate the complete set of literal-text occurrences in canonical source, returning stable source UTF-16 ranges, the total count, and a pagination cursor. Use when: Locate the first, previous, or every lexical occurrence before interpreting it. Do not use lexical exhaustiveness as proof of semantic exhaustiveness. Hits are data.occurrences: pass a hit's start_lid as book_text.lid and end_lid as book_text.end_lid; source_range_utf16 is the exact whole-hit range and ranges gives per-LID positions. Returns a built projection in data, not a generated answer. Collections are paged: data_path identifies a continuation's collection in the original projection and total_items its size. next_calls may include multiple collection branches and search batches. Concept matched_count/truncated still describe bounded candidate recall. Read chosen evidence LIDs with book_text. Missing built capability returns material_unavailable. Copy published_book_ref from book_list and check its available_tools. Costs 1 call on success, including empty results, each continuation page and repeated successful requests; failures cost 0. complete=false means more pages exist; copy needed next_calls name and arguments unchanged. sources gives published_book_ref, start_lid/end_lid, source_range and source_url: cite only evidence actually read, retaining its version and exact range. An empty sources array provides no source citation. usage is the server's post-call balance with charged_units and charged_from; do not infer balance locally. On quota_exhausted stop content retries and report usage.free_resets_at plus top_up_url or top_up_instruction; book_list and mcp_usage remain free.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the preceding search result. Omit or null for the first page; preserve query, match_mode, scope, order and page_size on continuation. A changed source revision invalidates it.

match_mode.description: exact (default) matches unchanged text; normalized applies NFKC, full non-Turkic case folding and whitespace collapsing. Both locate literal occurrences, not semantic equivalents; result ranges use original-source UTF-16 positions.

order.description: document (default) returns earliest occurrences first; reverse_document returns latest first. Uses canonical source order, not lexical LID sorting. Combine before with reverse_document for previous occurrences.

page.description: Copy a continuation from next_calls to read an omitted collection. data_path identifies its position in the full projection.

page_size.description: Maximum literal occurrences per search page, 1..50, default 20. Does not change total_occurrences or exhaustive coverage of the requested literal scope; preserve it when using cursor.

published_book_ref.description: Copy the exact immutable publication reference from book_list; keep both identifiers on every content call and continuation.

publication_id.description: Exact publication version returned by book_list.

query.description: Literal text to locate in canonical source, containing non-whitespace text and at most 4,096 Unicode scalar values. Exact mode preserves query whitespace; this is not a semantic question or regex. Read chosen hits using their start_lid/end_lid.

direction.description: before keeps hits ending at or before the reference span's start; after keeps hits starting at or after its end. Direction filters scope independently of result order.

lid.description: Known reference LID in this book. The relative filter excludes this node's entire source span, including its descendants.

relative_to.description: Optional before/after filter around a known LID, excluding that node's span. Intersects with within_lid when both are supplied.

within_lid.description: Known LID whose source span, including descendants, must contain each whole hit. Omit or null for no subtree restriction.

scope.description: Optional source scope using known LIDs from this book. Omit, null or {} searches the whole book; within_lid and relative_to intersect, and each whole hit must fit the resulting range.

tools.description: Check this account's server-calculated call balance before planning more reads or after quota_exhausted. Costs 0 calls, even when exhausted. Takes no arguments. Returns usage: free_remaining, paid_remaining, free_resets_at (next Hong Kong month), paid_next_expires_at and call_packs with per-batch expiry and available_units. Free credits are spent first, then valid packs by earliest expiry; all clients share this account's balance. charged_units is 0 and charged_from is null for this query. If both balances are zero, stop content retries and tell the user the reset time and top_up_url, or top_up_instruction when the URL is null. The user arranges purchase; a purchase does not grant material access. No evidence sources or continuation pages are returned.
